newsitem.title: USA: U.S. November cash hog prices set record high.
newsitem.headline: U.S. November cash hog prices set record high.

text.p: Average cash hog prices in the United States in November were $54.81 per hundredweight (CWT), a record for the month and above the previous high of $53.63 in November 1986, the National Pork Producers Council said.
Growing pork exports fed the price strength which occurred despite strong marketings of 7.6 million hogs, more than 22 percent higher than the 6.3 million marketed 10 years earlier.
Pork exports in the first nine months of 1996 rose 23 percent from a year earlier, while imports fell eight percent.

"Strong retail demand, widespread use of pork, especially bacon by fast-food operators, and high levels of competition by a larger, more efficient packing sector also contributed to the performance," NPPC director of economics Steve Meyer said.
NPPC said the data was based on research by Glenn Grimes, ag economist at the University of Missouri-Columbia. (Chicago newsdesk 312 408 8720)
